title: UCP alternative path: requires_escalation and handoff through continue_url
summary: The business needs something the API cannot collect, or a policy needs the buyer to approve the order. It returns requires_escalation with a continue_url and a message whose severity is requires_buyer_input or requires_buyer_review. The platform fixes any recoverable errors first, then opens continue_url, and the buyer finishes on the business UI.

steps.label: PUT /checkout-sessions/chk_456
steps.detail: The platform updates the checkout with the data it has.

steps.label: status requires_escalation + continue_url
steps.detail: requires_buyer_input means the checkout is incomplete because the business needs data its API cannot take. requires_buyer_review means the checkout is complete but a policy, such as a high-value order or a first purchase, needs the buyer to approve it. Either way continue_url must be an absolute HTTPS URL.

failures.outcome: The business broke a MUST; the platform cannot hand off and should treat the checkout as stuck.

steps.label: Resolve recoverable errors first
steps.detail: If the messages also hold recoverable errors, the platform fixes them with another update before handing off. The example error-processing algorithm in the spec checks requires_buyer_input before requires_buyer_review.

steps.label: Open continue_url for the buyer
steps.detail: The platform must use continue_url. The recommended form is an opaque URL backed by server-side state whose lifetime follows expires_at; a stateless checkout permalink is the alternative.

steps.label: Buyer finishes on the business UI
steps.detail: The buyer gives the missing data or approves the order on the merchant site. The business moves the session to completed.

failures.outcome: The session expires (default 6 hours) and becomes canceled.

steps.label: GET /checkout-sessions/chk_456
steps.detail: The platform reads the final state. A completed checkout carries the order and is immutable.
